ben-allen.text: Says there is "no silver bullet"; would strengthen the admitted market rather than replace it with a state program, reform rate review, expand risk reduction and data sharing, and stabilize the FAIR Plan.

source.title: Jane Kim's plan to remake California insurance draws fire as FAIR Plan increase nears (Insurance Business)

ben-allen.text: Would increase oversight and accountability of the FAIR Plan; require real-time reporting of claim delays and explanations for denials; appoint a consumer advocate.

source.title: CalMatters 2026 California Voter Guide: Insurance Commissioner

ben-allen.text: Opposes expanding the low-cost auto insurance program to all drivers.

source.title: CalMatters 2026 California Voter Guide: Insurance Commissioner

ben-allen.text: Authored Proposition 4 climate bond and restrictions on single-use plastics; says fossil fuel industry should be held accountable.

source.title: CalMatters 2026 California Voter Guide: Insurance Commissioner

ben-allen.text: Endorsed by Sierra Club, California Environmental Voters, California Professional Firefighters and the California Democratic Party.

source.title: CalMatters 2026 California Voter Guide: Insurance Commissioner

jane-kim.text: Proposes "Natural Disaster Insurance for All," a state-run nonprofit pool, plus minimum loss-ratio floors so insurers return more premium as claims.

source.title: Jane Kim's plan to remake California insurance draws fire as FAIR Plan increase nears (Insurance Business)

jane-kim.text: Would pay interest to policyholders for delayed, denied or underpaid claims and freeze rates during claims; create public dashboard of insurer records.

source.title: CalMatters 2026 California Voter Guide: Insurance Commissioner

jane-kim.text: Would audit the FAIR Plan committee and add seats for consumer advocates; expand low-cost auto insurance to all drivers.

source.title: Jane Kim's plan to remake California insurance draws fire as FAIR Plan increase nears (Insurance Business)

jane-kim.text: As San Francisco supervisor, secured free community college for city residents, the state's first $15 minimum wage ordinance and a tenant-protection ordinance against unjust evictions, according to CalMatters.
